tested:
Cisco ASA 9.1.5 "asa-915-k8" build (NPX-303, root-caused 2026-09-23) - a SEPARATE,
more specific key so this image does not inherit the "asa" profile's 384 MB RAM
ceiling above. That ceiling is correct ONLY for the ancient 8.0.2 image (2.6.17
kernel, GRUB-legacy initrd-placement bug - see the "asa" entry's own RAM CEILING
comment). This 9.1.5 build is a genuinely different kernel (2.6.29.6, direct
`kernel`/`initrd` boot lines, no legacy-GRUB stage2) and does NOT hit that bug -
live-boot evidence (in-platform, rule #58): at the "asa" profile's 384 MB cap it
unpacks its initramfs fine ("Unpacking initramfs... done", "383MB LOWMEM available")
and reaches real ASA userland startup, but then the `lina` process itself fails to
allocate its shared memory pool ("mempool: error 22 creating global shared pool")
and segfaults ("lina[499]: segfault at 0 ... in lina[8048000+273b000]"), rebooting in
a loop - a plain RAM-shortage crash, not the earlier "Timer not a leaf" signature
this device's PLATFORM-AUDIT row previously reported (that symptom came from a run
made before the NPX-153/NPX-1339 NIC + tcg/icount/smbios-drift fixes landed; it does
not reproduce under the now-current clean KVM + i82559er config at all). Per rule
59, EVE-NG's own asa.yml (single template, all classic-ASA versions) pins `ram:
2048` - this key restores that EVE-NG-parity value for the 9.1.5 build specifically,
instead of carrying the 8.0.2-only 384 MB deviation onto an image it actively harms.

reasons.kvm:
TIMER-SUBSYSTEM CRASH - ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED (NPX-303, 2026-09-23). Once this
image had enough RAM to get past the mempool crash above, it hit a SEPARATE,
later crash in its own timer subsystem - "(set_exptime) Timer not a leaf" /
"mgd_timer_set_exptime: Not a leaf" - soon after reaching a real login-capable
state. Live-tested in-platform (rule #58), narrowed by evidence, not guessed:
reproduced IDENTICALLY at 1024 MB and 2048 MB (not a RAM question), and under
BOTH plain KVM and per-node `kvm: False` (tcg) alone (not an accel question by
itself either). The guest kernel's own boot log showed a live TSC-instability
symptom on every boot ("Fast TSC calibration failed", "TSC: Unable to calibrate
against PIT", "Marking TSC unstable"). EVE-NG's real asa.yml runs the whole
classic-ASA family under `-icount 1` (deterministic virtual time, tcg-only -
QEMU refuses -icount together with KVM) - tested directly in-platform via the
per-node qemu_extra_args/kvm config keys (added `-icount` to qemu.py's SEC-24
extra-args allowlist to allow it): the SAME image that previously crashed at
this exact point now boots all the way to a real `ciscoasa>` prompt
("INFO: Power-On Self-Test complete." then the AnyConnect banner then the
prompt), confirmed via the raw serial.log, not the API's own interpretation.
Per rule #59, this is now the permanent, evidence-backed default for this
profile ONLY (asa-8.02 is untouched - it does not reach this code path at all,
since it panics on the RAM ceiling long before any timer code runs) - a plain
per-node override still wins if a future, faster-booting build of this same
image ever ships and no longer needs it.
